title: Stack Overflow
concept: Prevent stack overflow in recursive functions with depth-limit contracts and tail recursion — protecting against infinite recursion crashes.
why: Stack overflow crashes are hard to debug because the call stack is enormous and the actual bug (missing base case) is buried at the top.
tips: EVERY recursive function must have a base case — write it first
Prefer tail recursion — the compiler can optimize it to a loop
If you can't use tail recursion, add a depth parameter with a max-depth contract
For production code with deep recursion, prefer iterative solutions
common_mistakes: Writing recursive functions without base cases
Assuming tail-call optimization always happens — check the compiler output if depth is critical
Using recursion for problems with millions of iterations — use iteration instead
